sources.title: Enhancing dance learning by reducing cognitive load: A preregistered study on the effect of dancers’ viewing perspective and expertise
sources.authors: Versace E, Angioi M, Hadfield K, Gallo V, Jensen LJ, Roman J, Sheriff K, Redding E, Clarke F, Deering J, Morrissey D, Buckingham S.

findings.finding: A back view perspective consistently leads to better performance and movement accuracy, particularly for dancers with less experience.
findings.quote: The Back view consistently yielded superior outcomes, especially among less trained dancers.

findings.finding: First-person or back-view perspectives are more effective for learning because they lower the cognitive demand on the learner.
findings.quote: These findings suggest that first-person perspectives enhance motor learning by reducing cognitive load.

principle: Providing a back view perspective during instruction reduces cognitive load and improves motor learning outcomes compared to mirrored or front-facing views.
for_the_teacher: Use a back-facing camera angle when demonstrating new choreography to minimize the mental effort required for the learner to mirror your movements.
Prioritize first-person or back-view video demonstrations for beginners to improve their movement accuracy and spatial awareness.
when_it_does_not_apply: The study noted no significant performance differences between front mirror views and front opposite views, and results may vary based on the dancer's prior background or experience level.
